notes.title: We’re Locked, Loaded, and Submitted – Hillbilly Hellfire Launching Soon!
notes.content:
The time has come. After months of demon-smashing, turret-tweaking, and meth-lab-refining (in lore, obviously), I'm proud to say that Hillbilly Hellfire has been officially submitted for review on Steam.

That’s right—the game is done.
Barring any surprises during the review process, we are aiming for a June release.

This wouldn’t be possible without the incredible support from all of you—
✅ Everyone who wishlisted the game
✅ Everyone who played the demo
✅ Everyone who dropped feedback, bug reports, and encouragement in along the way

You helped shape this game, and I truly hope you have as much fun playing it as I did building it.

🛠️ What’s in the Final Build?
Full progression and upgrade system

Multiple maps with unique layouts and choke points

Endless mode, boss fights, and plenty of explosions

A full arsenal of heavenly weapons and turret traps

And of course, plenty of ridiculous unlockable cosmetics to bless your inner Skeeter

⏳ What’s Next?
We’re just waiting for the green light from Steam.
Once approved, I’ll drop a full release date announcement and start rolling out launch trailers, patch notes, and rewards for early supporters.

Until then:
👉 Wishlist if you haven’t already
👉 Tell a friend, stream it, or share the demo
👉 Join the Discord and hang out—we're having fun over there

Thank you again for being part of this wild ride.
We’re almost there.

— Slagathor 🧢
Solo Dev, Chicken Wrangler, Demon-Slayer-in-Chief

notes.title: The Hillbilly Hellfire Demo is Here
notes.content:
Where to start? i soft-launched the demo last week, and the response has been absolutely incredible. The number of Wishlists we’ve received has been overwhelming, and I just want to say THANK YOU to everyone who’s taken the time to check out Hillbilly Hellfire.

I sincerely hope you enjoy playing it as much as I enjoyed making it—this game has been a wild ride from day one, and seeing people actually playing and having fun means the world to me.

Now, I want to take a second to address a question I’ve been seeing a lot:

Why is saving disabled?
Hillbilly Hellfire is meant to be a short, high-intensity experience, especially in the demo. The goal isn’t to have players binging it for hours—it’s just a taste of the full game, which I’m planning to release in March. If you’re enjoying it that much, that’s awesome (seriously, I love you for that), but there are tons of other great demos out right now—go check them out!

Some of my personal favorites so far have been:

🛡️ Stronghold Crusaders by FireFly – Classic castle-building, but better than ever.
🌀 Twisted Tower by Thomas Brush & 3D Realms – A punchy, playful, yet dark homage to Bioshock that oozes ATMOSphere.

So go try some demos, have fun, and maybe come back and try another round of Hillbilly Hellfire when its ready for you to blast some more demons.

What’s Next?
The full release is planned for March—I’ll share more details soon!
Keep the feedback coming—I’m already looking at tweaks and improvements.
If you haven’t yet, Wishlist the game on Steam—it helps more than you know!
Once again, thank you for the amazing support. Now go fire up the demo, lock n’ load, and remember—keep your turrets loaded and your powder dry. 🔥

Agenda:

Development Highlights

Roadmap and Next Steps

Steam Next Fest demo release.
Further development goals.
Call for wishlist additions and feedback.

Closing Remarks
Gratitude to the community.
Reminder to follow, wishlist, and join the Discord.
Tease of future streams and updates.


Patch Notes:
•	Spent most of the week addressing feedback from the latest playtest.

Worked extensively on the Cinematics Module:
•	Achieved the functionality needed for my vision, but the learning curve was significant.
•	Focused on capturing additional footage from the three environments created so far.

•	Remade the trailer with improved visuals and pacing.

•	Fixed skeleton geometry collections for more satisfying and dynamic explosions.

Implemented various UI improvements:
•	Health bar: Reduced its size for a cleaner HUD.
•	Round timer: Switched from numerical display to a slider for better visual clarity.

Encountered a major issue with screen resolution scaling:
•	A catastrophic bug nearly derailed progress.
•	ChatGPT helped solve the issue, saving hours of frustration.

•	Still iterating on the progression system
